Proof in the paper: The lattice fringe space of 2.76 and 2.65 Å all corresponding to the NiS2 (200) plane. A slight contraction appeared compared to that of pure NiS2 (d (200) = 2.83 Å), which was most possibly caused by the substitution of Co and V atoms for Ni in the lattice sites of the NiS2 matrix. Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns further confirmed the existence of the NiS2 (200) plane. The energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mappings of NCVS-3 provided direct-viewing evidence for the uniform distribution of Ni, Co, V, and S elements.
